title: What an unscoped enumerator really is

prereqs.why: The output is the numbering rule plus the implicit conversion to int, which are the two things an unscoped enum does.
The values are integers, and that is the point — the names are a thin layer over them.

statement:
**What does this print?** Four lines.

Two rules decide all of it: how the numbering works when you set some values and not others, and what an enumerator turns into when you use it where a number is expected.
hints: The first enumerator is 0 unless you say otherwise, and each one after it is one more than the one before — including after an explicit value.
`std::cout << red` compiles. Think about what type `red` has to become for that to work, and what gets printed as a result.
